answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from a tide-linked bonding schedule: each new identity must post a stake that rises and falls with the overall participation tide, forcing an attacker who floods fakes to lock capital across a rising knoll of required deposits. A sudden gale of coordinated registrations triggers an automatic stake multiplier, so the cost of sustaining a sybil swarm scales faster than honest agents single deposits, making large-scale identity farming economically painful.
